learn.hook: Before phones, travellers wrote letters — and a single letter could carry a whole journey inside it!
points: 'North, South, East, West' is a lesson made of letters written from different parts of India. Here we learn to write such letters.
An informal letter is written to family or friends in a warm, chatty style.
Parts of an informal letter: sender's address, date, salutation (Dear Anu,), body, closing (With love,) and name.
A formal letter (to a principal or an officer) uses 'Sir/Madam', a subject line and a closing like 'Yours sincerely'.
Travel letters describe places, food, weather, people and feelings. P.S. (postscript) adds a note after the letter ends.

example.q: Read: Dear Anu, Greetings from Shillong! It rained three times today, and the hills wore a cap of clouds. We ate hot momos near the market. I wish you were here! With love, Tara. P.S. I'm bringing you a pineapple! Find the salutation, the closing and the postscript.
steps: 'With love, Tara' ends the letter → closing and name.
'P.S. I'm bringing you a pineapple!' is added at the end → postscript.
example.answer: Salutation: 'Dear Anu,' — Closing: 'With love, Tara' — Postscript: 'P.S. I'm bringing you a pineapple!'

learn.reallife: Emails and holiday messages follow the same idea: greet, share your news, close warmly.

games.title: Spot the part
pairs: We reached Kochi this morning by train.

quiz.q: In a letter, 'Dear Anu,' is the:
quiz.explain: The salutation is the greeting that begins the letter.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the greeting with the ending

quiz.q: Which closing suits an informal letter to a friend?
quiz.explain: 'With love' is warm and suits family and friends.
quiz.mistake: Uses a formal closing in a friendly letter

quiz.q: In a letter, the main part that carries your news is called the:
quiz.explain: The body is where you share your news and feelings.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the greeting holds the main message

quiz.q: A letter to your school principal asking for leave is a:
quiz.explain: Letters to officials such as a principal are formal.
quiz.mistake: Treats every letter as informal

quiz.q: 'Dear Anu, Greetings from Shillong! It rained three times today.' Where is Tara writing from?
quiz.explain: She says 'Greetings from Shillong!'
quiz.mistake: Does not read the opening line carefully

quiz.q: 'The hills wore a cap of clouds.' What does this tell us?
options: Clouds were resting on the tops of the hills
quiz.explain: A cap sits on top of a head, so the clouds were sitting on the hilltops.
quiz.mistake: Reads the description literally

quiz.q: Where is the date usually written in a letter?
options: near the top, below the sender's address
after the writer's name at the end
quiz.explain: The date comes at the top, just below the sender's address.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the format of a letter

quiz.q: What does 'P.S.' at the end of a letter mean?
options: a note added after the letter is finished
quiz.explain: P.S. stands for postscript — something added after signing off.
quiz.mistake: Guesses the short form

teach.ask: Gappu is writing to his cousin from his trip. What parts does a friendly letter need?
teach.praise: Dear Cousin, greetings from the treetops! With love, Gappu. Perfect!
teach.nudge: How does a letter begin, and how does it end?

learn.hook: Travel from Ladakh to Kanyakumari and you'll pass snow, deserts, rainforests and beaches — all in one country!
points: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
North: Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh have the high Himalayan mountains.
South: Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka; Kanyakumari is at the southern tip of mainland India.
East and North-east: West Bengal, Odisha and Assam; Bihu is celebrated in Assam. West: Gujarat and Rajasthan; the Thar Desert lies mostly in Rajasthan.
Culture means a group's way of life — food, language, clothes, festivals, music and dance.

example.q: Tara writes from Assam, Arjun from Kerala and Kiran from Rajasthan. Which direction of India is each in?
example.answer: Tara — North-east, Arjun — South, Kiran — West

learn.reallife: Indian railways connect all four directions; a long journey shows you new foods, languages and dances at every station.

quiz.q: The sun rises in the:
quiz.explain: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up east and west

quiz.q: Kanyakumari is at India's:
quiz.explain: Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu is the southernmost point of mainland India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where Kanyakumari is

quiz.q: Bihu is a festival and dance of:
quiz.explain: Bihu is celebrated in Assam.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up regional festivals

quiz.q: The Thar Desert lies mostly in:
quiz.explain: Most of the Thar Desert is in western Rajasthan.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the desert to the west of India

quiz.q: Kathakali is a classical dance from:
quiz.explain: Kathakali, with its colourful make-up, comes from Kerala.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up classical dances

quiz.q: Which of these states is in the far west of India?
quiz.explain: Gujarat is on India's western coast. The others are in the North-east.
quiz.mistake: Confuses east and west

quiz.q: Which direction is exactly opposite to north-east?
quiz.explain: Opposite of north is south and opposite of east is west, so north-east ↔ south-west.
quiz.mistake: Changes only one half of the direction

quiz.q: What does 'culture' mean?
options: only the weather of a place
the way of life of a group — food, language, festivals and arts
the number of people in a city
quiz.explain: Culture is how people live, celebrate and express themselves.
quiz.mistake: Confuses culture with geography

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly across India. Tell him about the four directions and one thing from different parts of India.
teach.praise: North for snow, south for beaches, west for deserts, east for tea gardens — let's fly!
teach.nudge: Can you name the four directions and something from each?

learn.hook: Over the bridge, through the tunnel, along the river — tiny words guide every journey!
points: A preposition shows how a noun or pronoun is related to another word, often by place, direction or time.
Place: in, on, under, between, beside, near, behind, at.
Direction or movement: to, towards, into, across, along, through, up, down.
'In' shows position inside; 'into' shows movement from outside to inside.
'Between' is used for two people or things; 'among' for more than two.

example.q: Fill the blanks: 'The ferry went ___ the river, and we walked ___ the bank to the temple.'
steps: Going from one side to the other side → across
Moving beside the length of the bank → along

learn.reallife: Maps, signboards and GPS directions use prepositions: 'Turn left at the signal, go across the bridge.'

items.text: The cat is hiding ___ the bed.
The children ran ___ the park towards the gate.

games.title: Preposition rules
items: 'Between' is used for two people or things.
'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.
'Among' is used for exactly two things.
'Among' is for more than two; 'between' is for two.
In 'The cat is under the bed', 'under' is a preposition.
It shows where the cat is.
'Quickly' is an adverb; it tells how something is done.

quiz.q: 'The boat sailed ___ the river to the other bank.'
quiz.explain: Across means from one side to the other.
quiz.mistake: Picks a place word instead of a direction word

quiz.q: 'The cat ran ___ the house when it started raining.'
quiz.explain: 'Into' shows movement from outside to inside.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the movement preposition

quiz.q: 'The ball is ___ the table and the chair.'
quiz.explain: Two things are named, so we use 'between'.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'among' for two things

quiz.q: 'Share the sweets ___ all your classmates.'
quiz.explain: There are many classmates (more than two), so 'among' is correct.
quiz.mistake: Uses 'between' for a big group

quiz.q: 'We waited ___ the bus stop for half an hour.'
quiz.explain: 'At' is used for a particular point or place like a bus stop.
quiz.mistake: Uses a movement preposition for a fixed point

quiz.q: 'My cousin lives ___ Kolkata.'
quiz.explain: We use 'in' for cities and countries.
quiz.mistake: Uses a preposition that shows movement or surface

quiz.q: 'The train went ___ a long tunnel.'
quiz.explain: 'Through' means in at one end and out at the other.
quiz.mistake: Does not picture the movement

quiz.q: 'Walk ___ the river bank to reach the temple.'
quiz.explain: 'Along' means moving beside the length of something.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up along and among

teach.ask: Gappu is lost! Explain prepositions so he can follow directions like 'across the bridge' and 'along the road'.
teach.praise: Across the bridge, along the road, into my nest — home at last!
teach.nudge: What do prepositions tell us — about place or direction?
